items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I could make a case for somebody being interested in Lester Young, which I'm not, but I can understand something of that.

ctx.x: You don't understand the basis of his appeal?

Not at all. I don't know why anybody's interested in Charlie Parker. I could make a case for somebody being interested in Lester Young, which I'm not, but I can understand something of that. But I just can't understand it.

No, what happened with Charlie Parker is that, to a certain extent, he became a romantic hero of the beat generation. Oh, yes. Ferlinghetti, all the New York beat things. Now, the question as to why he did is somehow they read into his music a lot of protest themes. And, of course, you can take any musician's thing and read anything you wanted to it. But it's interesting that he became a kind of a basis for a romantic legend the same way Bix did. That is, in New York and Subway Walls, you'd have Bird Lives.
